question:
Select the most appropriate option to improve the bold part of the sentence.

You must** refrain to smoke.**
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The verb "**refrain**" is always followed by "**from**" when referring to avoiding or abstaining from something.
 
• Using "refrain to smoke" is incorrect because "to" does not pair with "refrain" in this context.
 
• The correct phrase is "**refrain from smoking**," which ensures grammatical accuracy.
 
• Thus, the bold part of the sentence should be replaced with **Option 4**.

Therefore, the correct answer is **Option 4**.

 

**Correct Sentence:** *"You must refrain from smoking."*

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: "quit from smoke"** – This is incorrect because "quit" does not require "from" and "smoke" should be changed to "smoking" for proper usage.
 
• **Option 2: "stop to smoke"** – This is incorrect because "stop" should be followed by "smoking" (gerund) rather than "to smoke" (infinitive) in this context.
 
• **Option 3: "stop of smoking"** – This is incorrect because "stop" is not paired with "of" in standard English usage.
